newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy probes claims soldiers tortured in Somalia.
newsitem.headline: Italy probes claims soldiers tortured in Somalia.

text.p: Italy said on Thursday it was investigating allegations that its soldiers tortured Somalis while on a peace-keeping mission in 1993.
The army chief of staff's office said in a statement that an inquiry was under way into a photo-report due to be published in Friday's edition of weekly news magazine Panorama.
The report uses photographs alleged to have been taken by Michele Patruno between April and May, 1993. Patruno was a member of a parachute regiment sent to Somalia at the time.

Panorama said the photographs showed prisoners tied and hooded and in once case, an officer preparing to apply electrodes to a Somali man's testicles. Some of the photographs were shown on television news broadcasts.
The alleged torture was carried out to encourage Somalis to reveal the presence of armed groups or weapons or other people," Patruno told state television RAI.
"There's a dose of sadism, maybe things didn't have to go so far," he said, adding that he had been told by colleagues that some Somalis had died as a result.
Military prosecutor Antonino Intelisano told RAI that investigations had been carried out in 1993 after some photographs surfaced, but no charges were brought.
Defence Undersecretary Massimo Brutti confirmed that an inquiry was under way and said he wanted to study the Panorama report carefully.
He said that if the allegations proved to be true "there can be no indulgence". But he added: "The whole case must be analysed and understood thoroughly. Why has this been denounced so late?"
General Domenico Corcione, defence chief of staff at the time of Italy's operation in Somalia, said he was amazed.
"I exclude any form of maltreatment of Somali prisoners by our soldiers," he said. "It is unimaginable."
